subject: OpalTech late-stage: probe on dedicated GPU availability and staggered allocation plan
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: OpalTech late-stage: quick availability probe

Hi Monica / Lauren,

OpalTech is in legal review and we just got a verbal confirmation that they want to proceed if we can guarantee coverage for the first 3 months of the Dedicated plan. Their POC starts the week of June 10 and they want deterministic GPU throughput for batch inference during burst windows.

Can you do a fast availability check for June/July across our us-west and us-east Dedicated pools? I need an estimate for:
- peak concurrent GPUs we can reserve for 6-week blocks
- a shorthold (soft hold) option so we can guarantee without long-term commitment immediately
- any collision with already-scheduled onboarding windows for Q2 clients

I'll loop in the OpalTech procurement contact once we have a sketch. This is late-stage — they asked for a tentative hold while legal finishes.

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OpalTech late-stage: quick availability probe

Rishi —

Quick summary after checking allocations and the ops calendar: attached a short snapshot (opaltech_capacity_snapshot_may27.pdf). Highlights:

- us-west (primary): We can provide a soft hold for up to 40 A100-equivalent GPUs for the June 10–July 21 window if we stagger activation across two clusters (cluster-w-03 and cluster-w-07). That would keep tail latency guarantees intact for existing tenants.
- us-east (secondary failover): We have 12 GPUs that can be reserved for cold failover; warm-up time is ~3 hours for model cache priming.
- Conflict windows: Two onboarding jobs are scheduled June 11–13 on cluster-w-03 (small batch training jobs) — we can shift one job to cluster-w-09 if we accept a 6-hour maintenance window.

Soft hold approach: ops can mark capacity as "soft-reserved" for up to 10 business days, during which we won't reassign to other late-stage deals. After that, it releases unless we convert to a commitment. Staging the hold across clusters reduces single-point risk.

I've attached a proposed staggered allocation plan spreadsheet (staggered-allocation-proposal-v1.xlsx) that outlines activation days and cache priming slots. If OpalTech wants a stricter SLA or hard-commit, we'll need a 30-day lead and a contract amendment for reserved capacity.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Rishi: tell OpalTech we can provide a 10-day soft hold on the 40 GPUs in us-west + 12 in us-east failover and ask for exact POC peak hours.
2) Lauren: can you confirm pricing delta for soft-hold vs committed reserve (monthly pricing + premium) and any SLA exceptions?
3) Ops: I'll tentatively block the clusters pending confirmation of the maintenance shift.

Monica

-- 
Monica Patel

From: Priya Bhattacharjee <priya@opaltech.ai>

Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 14:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: OpalTech late-stage: quick availability probe

Thanks Rishi / Monica — this is helpful.

OpalTech is targeting June 10 start for a 4-week POC with an expected burst pattern: 4am–8am PT and 4pm–6pm PT daily (batch inference spikes). We would like to request a tentative soft hold while our legal/compliance finishes the MSA — ideally until June 7.

Two asks:
1) Can you confirm warm-start time and whether the cache-priming window can be automated for the first day?
2) If we accept a soft-hold with the option to convert to a committed reserve, what is the delta to convert on short notice (within 72 hours)?

We appreciate the staggered cluster approach if it reduces single-point failures — we'd prefer primary + failover in different regions if possible.

Priya

-- 
Priya Bhattacharjee
Head of Platform Engineering
OpalTech
priya@opaltech.ai

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Priya Bhattacharjee <priya@opaltech.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2029 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OpalTech late-stage: quick availability probe

Priya —

Thanks for the details. Short answers:

- Warm-start/cache priming: We can automate the warm-start sequence. Ops will run a scripted cache priming job that pulls the model artifacts and runs a quick validation suite. It typically completes in 2–3 hours for the model sizes you described; we'll reserve a 4-hour window the first day to be safe.
- Conversion delta: If you convert a soft-hold to a committed reserve within 72 hours, the pricing delta is the monthly committed rate pro-rated plus a 10% expedited conversion surcharge (this covers re-prioritization of capacity and permanent mapping). Exact numbers: committed monthly rate for 40 A100-equivalent GPUs = $312,000/month; pro-rated for remaining month + 10% surcharge. I can get finance to give a precise pro-rate once you confirm exact start date.

Operational plan (proposal):
- Place a 10-day soft hold on 40 GPUs in us-west (cluster-w-03 & cluster-w-07 staggered) + 12 GPUs in us-east as cold failover.
- Schedule an automated 4-hour priming window on June 10 at 03:00 PT.
- Shift the small onboarding job from cluster-w-03 to cluster-w-09 and mark a 6-hour maintenance on June 11 (ops will coordinate).

Rishi: please confirm with Priya that they want the soft hold through June 7 and if they want finance to run the exact pro-rate so we can include it in the DocuSign package. If yes, I'll open a soft-hold ticket and attach the pricing worksheet.

Best,
Lauren
